holes_found.description: Cross-WIN inconsistency in `code_analysis.post_hoc` tagging. WIN-031 (North Pole cosmic mountain, Unfalsifiable, theological retrodiction from six ancient texts) is tagged `post_hoc: false` with the explanatory note 'Unfalsifiable theological claim ... No empirical observation exists to be post-hoc about. The prediction/retrodiction distinction does not apply to unfalsifiable assertions.' WIN-032 (New Jerusalem pole axis, Unfalsifiable, theological retrodiction from Revelation 21) is tagged `post_hoc: true` because 'the claim references Revelation 21 (~1st century CE)'. These are structurally identical: both are theological claims where an ancient text is mapped onto the pole axis. Whichever tagging rule is correct, one of them is wrong. A dome defender pointing at Part 3.1a's per-tag definitions can force us to justify why our own tag application is inconsistent — undermining the classification apparatus that Parts 2b and 3.1a lean on.
holes_found.recommendation: Pick one rule and apply it to both. Option A: adopt WIN-031's logic — 'post_hoc doesn't apply to Unfalsifiable claims' — and re-tag WIN-032 to `post_hoc: false` with matching evidence text. Option B: adopt WIN-032's logic — 'reference to an ancient text is retrodictive by definition' — and re-tag WIN-031 to `post_hoc: true`. Option A is cleaner because it preserves the semantic content of the tag (retrodiction vs prospective, which presupposes an observable); Option B risks making `post_hoc: true` mean two different things across the taxonomy. Regardless of which option is chosen, whichever WIN is retagged should carry a note in its `post_hoc_evidence` explaining the categorical decision so future reviewers can't relitigate this inconsistency.

holes_found.description: Missed opportunity: the detail_verdict_text argues that WIN-032 fails 'under the dome author's own definition and our stricter standard in Part 3.1b,' but does NOT quote the author's own definition inline. The definition ('Prospective = prediction was timestamped before confirming data was pulled. Not retrofitted. Not explained after the fact. Predicted, then verified.') lives in Part 3.1b's author-quote blockquote. A reader who hasn't read Part 3.1b has to trust the reference. Pulling the four-word phrase 'Predicted, then verified' inline into WIN-032's paragraph would strengthen the scorecard-composition argument by grounding it in the author's own self-imposed standard: WIN-032 cannot be verified at all — no observation exists that would confirm a supernatural pole-axis descent — so it fails on the author's own terms, not just ours.

holes_found.description: Carry-over from c6 hole #7 (three-untestable grouping) — STILL PRESENT. detail_verdict_text's advocate-response paragraph groups 'pre-CMB cosmology, black-hole interiors, or string-theoretic vacua' as examples of 'currently untestable' mainstream claims that the dome defender could invoke asymmetrically. These have quite different scientific statuses: pre-CMB cosmology has measurable indirect signatures (baryon asymmetry, BBN abundances, primordial GW bounds); black-hole interiors are strict GR consequences with no external handle; string-theoretic vacua are a theory-space problem. Per PROP-047 §5a re-grep: exact phrase 'pre-CMB cosmology, black-hole interiors, or string-theoretic vacua' is present in current data/wins.json HEAD; no intervening ISS since c6 (2026-04-18) touched this grouping. A physicist-adjacent dome defender could use the grouping to undermine the paragraph's precision — 'you lumped together three things with very different scientific standing, so your inverse-position claim needs to be re-scoped.'
holes_found.recommendation: Narrow the example to 'black-hole interiors' alone — that is the tightest structural analogy to WIN-032's position (a strict consequence of the framework's core commitments with no measurable external handle). The one-word simplification closes the hole. Alternatively add a parenthetical disclaimer ('though these differ in the degree to which indirect signatures exist') that acknowledges the differences without a rewrite.

advocate_mode.best_defense: A serious dome defender would not attack our Unfalsifiable verdict directly — the pole-axis claim really is unfalsifiable, and defending its inclusion in a scientific scorecard is not the strongest ground. Instead they would attack the framing that our review's reader will encounter FIRST: the summary table entry ('Theological assertion, not testable physical claim'). The defender would argue: 'This is a category error on YOUR part. WIN-032's function in the dome cosmology is not to make a physical prediction — it's to anchor the model in a specific theological framework. The dome author has been transparent about this from V50 forward: the model is not just a physics model, it is a physics-plus-eschatology synthesis, and its CONFIRMED tag on WIN-032 doesn't mean 'verified against measurement' but 'consistent with the model's stated theological wrapper.' Your review conflates the author's use of CONFIRMED-as-consistency-with-theological-frame with your desired use of CONFIRMED-as-verified-by-measurement. The disagreement is semantic, not scientific.' The paragraph's existing kernel-of-truth acknowledgment addresses this partially, but the summary-table row and TLDR both frame the WIN as if the author is confused about categories, rather than deploying a different (albeit non-scientific) definition of CONFIRMED. A charitable framing would separate 'author's stated definition' from 'scorecard math' more sharply: the dome scorecard is arithmetically a claim about predictive accuracy (69/69 = coverage-plus-verification), and the arithmetic requires homogeneous entries, whether or not the author frames each entry consistently.
advocate_mode.preemptive_recommendation: Add a single sentence to detail_verdict_text making the definitional split explicit: 'We do not dispute that the dome author uses CONFIRMED to mean consistent with the model's theological framework rather than verified against measurement; we dispute that a scorecard reporting an arithmetic accuracy percentage can mix entries under two different definitions of CONFIRMED without inflating the numerator.' This preempts the semantic-disagreement defense by conceding the semantics and pivoting to the arithmetic. It should slot in after the existing sentence about 'the dome author is free to define CONFIRMED as consistent with the model's theological wrapper' — that sentence sets up the concession but doesn't complete the pivot.

cross_win_consistency.inconsistencies_found: TWO cross-WIN issues, one substantive and one signposting. (1) SUBSTANTIVE — the `code_analysis.post_hoc` tag disagreement between WIN-031 and WIN-032 for structurally identical theological retrodictions is captured as the moderate hole above; will not repeat here. (2) SIGNPOSTING — WIN-024's post-2026-06-20 rewrite (ISS-2869, closed 2026-06-20T02:23Z) cites WIN-032 as an 'asymmetry hypothesis' the dome could invoke to explain the wind-belt vs SAA mismatch: 'Even granting the dome's own asymmetry hypotheses (WIN-030 elliptical disc, WIN-032 New Jerusalem axis) ...'. WIN-032's own panel does not mention that its pole-axis claim has been drafted into service as a candidate asymmetry mechanism elsewhere in the review. This is a missed cross-link: the WIN-032 panel could note that even under the most charitable steelman elsewhere in the review (WIN-024 grants the pole-axis as a candidate physical mechanism), the resulting attempt to unify wind-belt uniformity and SAA localization fails on kinematics — reinforcing WIN-032's own Unfalsifiable verdict from the outside. Not required for correctness, but a low-cost integration that strengthens the network of arguments. Recommendation: consider adding one sentence to WIN-032 detail_verdict_text noting the WIN-024 cross-usage and that even the maximally-charitable physical reading fails.

kernel_of_truth.description: The dome author's frame genuinely does unify theology and cosmology as a single coherent picture — WIN-032 is not a scientific mistake so much as a category-mixing deployment of a scorecard that the author intends to represent 'coverage of a unified model' rather than 'accuracy against measurement.' On the author's own terms, listing WIN-032 as CONFIRMED reflects internal consistency with the theological wrapper. Our own Part 3.1b's smoking-gun analysis (data/sections.json part3 posthoc-standard block) and the WIN-032 panel's kernel-of-truth paragraph already acknowledge this concession explicitly.
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: A scorecard that reports an arithmetic accuracy percentage (e.g., '69/69 CONFIRMED') is doing arithmetic, and arithmetic on heterogeneous entries produces a meaningless quotient. The dome author's home-page definition (data/sections.json part3 blockquote: 'Predicted, then verified') sets the operational standard: for CONFIRMED to mean anything in the numerator, each entry has to be verifiable. WIN-032 is not verifiable at all — no observation exists that would count as verifying a supernatural pole-axis descent. The author is free to publish a theology-and-physics manifesto; they are not free to report accuracy statistics that treat non-verifiable entries as if they had been verified. This gap is what the current WIN-032 panel calls 'the category error' — internal frame consistency and quantitative accuracy reporting cannot coexist without splitting the scorecard.

deeper_analysis:
Two-and-a-half months since c6 has been a good stretch for WIN-032 — 4 of 7 minor c6 holes have been retired by intervening decider patches (a decent hit rate for a low-priority WIN outside the priority queue). The verdict remains solidly Unfalsifiable and the argument survives fresh adversarial scrutiny. The strongest remaining line of attack is not in the WIN's own text but in the classification apparatus around it — the WIN-031/WIN-032 `post_hoc` inconsistency is a genuine hole because it is exactly the kind of thing a hostile reviewer can point to and ask 'if you cannot apply your own tags consistently to two structurally identical claims, why should we trust the aggregate counts in Part 2b?' That is the moderate finding. The minor findings are (a) an inline-quote opportunity that would materially strengthen the scorecard-composition argument by grounding it in the author's own words, and (b) two persistent minor c6 holes (monitor.py duplication, three-untestable grouping) that have been untouched by any ISS since c6 — legitimate persistence, per PROP-047 §5a re-grep of the current wins.json. The advocate-mode defense that survives at 3/5 (semantic-vs-arithmetic-definition of CONFIRMED) is closable in one sentence and would harden the paragraph against the strongest steelman a dome defender could construct.

On the tag-inconsistency finding: Option A (re-tag WIN-032 to `post_hoc: false`) is likely preferred because the semantic content of the `post_hoc` tag presupposes an observable to be post-hoc about; applying it to Unfalsifiable claims stretches the tag's meaning. Additionally, a `post_hoc: false` tag on WIN-032 would leave `derives_from_dome: false` and `monitoring: none` and `verdict: Unfalsifiable` intact — the WIN would remain a clear negative on the aggregate Part 2b counts without needing to add a fifth category to the tag apparatus.
